request: More melting and charring; retain the independently generated structural composition of the two large wrecks.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the provided top-down large mechanical wreck sprite. Preserve its exact composition, irregular silhouette, projecting structural fragments, major missing chunks, transparency, overhead camera, and hierarchy of a few huge structural masses with sparse tiny remains. DO NOT turn it into a circular pile and do not add small repeated parts.

CHANGE ONLY THE SEVERITY OF HEAT DAMAGE. The GM asks for substantially more MELTING AND CHARRING, not merely torn grey metal. This wreck was cooked through in an extreme machine fire after an internal blast. Make most exposed surfaces deeply charred charcoal-black, soot-grey and scorched dark brown, with only a few dull exposed silver metal scars. Large plates retain their mass but have sagged and wrinkled from heat; several torn edges should have partially liquefied into thick rounded irregular drips and cooled frozen metal runs. Visible blistering and bubbling of the metal skin, melted corners, a few heat-opened jagged apertures, crumpled blackened scale. The smaller inner mechanisms are largely fused into black clotted slag and tangled scorched wire, with most clean copper covered by soot. Some details have collapsed and welded to adjacent pieces, rather than looking neatly disassembled. Burned remnants of the original paint are dark, flaky and sparse.
Keep clear value contrast: muted ash-grey ridges and a few cool dull metallic edge highlights distinguish the large charred surfaces and deep cavities at token size. Show different materials physically ruined by heat. Everything is fully COOLED and inert: no active flames, glowing metal, embers, smoke, steam or sparks.
Preserve the existing broad plate surfaces and large structural fragments as dominant shapes. Keep the same alpha background and empty gaps, no floor, no background, no external shadow, no crater or separate debris field, no text, no extra machine anatomy. Transparent output. The result must read as MELTED AND CHARRED large-machine remains, while the same major masses and asymmetrical outline remain recognizable.
